newsitem.title: FRANCE: MAS to reduce ex-Paris cargo capacity.
newsitem.headline: MAS to reduce ex-Paris cargo capacity.

text.p: The decision by Malaysian Air System Bhd (MAS) to change the type of aircraft it operates between Paris and Kuala Lumpur will significantly reduce cargo capacity on the route, a Paris-based MAS cargo official told Reuters.

MAS currently operates three Boeing 747-400 combi fights per week on the Paris-Kuala Lumpur route. Two of the frequencies make a stopover in Munich for which the Paris cargo station has an allocation of 25 tonnes per flight.
The third frequency, added in June 1996, is non-stop and provides around 40-tonnes of ex-Paris capacity to Kuala Lumpur.

"MAS has decided to replace the combis with 747 passenger aircraft, effective March 8, 1997 while maintaining the same number of frequencies which will cut cargo capacity on the route by about 50 percent," the official said.
The move was part of an MAS strategy to re-deploy its 747 combis in Asia with the majorty of ex-Europe cargo being transported aboard freighters.

For the summer season, MAS planned to replace the 747 PAX with a 777 aircraft on the Paris-Kuala Lumpur whose cargo capacity, with a full passenger compliment, was limited to approximately 12 tonnes, the official added.

"In order to avoid being seriously downgraded as a cargo staion, we hope to recover the loss of cargo capacity by being allocated more space on the airline's 747F service between Amsterdam and Kuala Lumpur and will know more following a group level meeting of MAS cargo officials scheduled for next month," the MAS official said.
The Amsterdam freighter service is also used by MAS stations in the Benelux, Sweden and the UK. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
